locator.text: Display 120.5, p. 120, in the proof of Lemma 10.3

evidence: paper: b_j \;=\; \min\left\{\, b \in \mathbb{N} \;:\; b > b_{j-1}, \quad \max_{\substack{a,m \ge 0 \\ a+m \le \lfloor j/2 \rfloor}} C_{j,m}\, b^{\,m-j}\, \|F_j\|_{C^{a}} \le 2^{-j} \,\right\},

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Same device, a different formula. Lean takes no minimum over a constraint set: localScale j is an arbitrary natural above 2^j · boundSum j, produced by Classical.choose from the Archimedean property (exists_nat_gt), and boundSum j = Σ_{m<j} Σ_{k<j} templateBound m j k SUMS the template constants instead of maximizing C_{j,m} b^{m-j}‖F_j‖_{C^a}; the paper's b^{m-j} factor is not inside Lean's defining inequality at all, it is used afterwards through power_ratio_le (b^k/b^j ≤ 1/b for k < j). The paper's requirement b_j > b_{j-1} is then imposed separately by scale = DiagonalScale.doublingEnvelope localScale, which is strictly monotone and in addition at least doubles at each step (2 * scale j ≤ scale (j+1)) — a condition the paper does not ask for. The conclusion the paper draws from its choice, that the quantity bounded in (10.12) is at most 2^{-j}, is localized_derivative_tail_bound, but over the index range m < j and k < j (spatial window index and total joint derivative order) rather than the paper's a + m ≤ ⌊j/2⌋; both ranges exhaust every fixed order as j grows, which is all the tail argument needs. Lean also has no b_0 = 1 normalization: doublingEnvelope at 0 is max 1 (localScale 0).
